Commentary.Commentary: That is it from us then! End of a wonderful tournament and we have thoroughly enjoyed bringing it to you. Hope that you enjoyed it as well. We take your leave but before leaving, want to let you know that you could browse the tabs for scores from other international matches. A lot happening over the weekend. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Right then! Complete domination from the outset. That has been Team India. They made a statement in the very first game, beating Australia by a huge margin and in every match since, they have stamped their authority. Things only look more than bright for their future. As far as Australia are concerned, won't say that it was a one-off night. The gulf between the two sides is really big and unless India themselves threw it away, it was always going to be difficult for the Aussies to win. But credit to them for making it to the final and putting up some fight. Sometimes you learn a lot from defeats, so this could shape their future in a nice manner.

Victorious Indian skipper, Prithvi Shaw says that he cannot express what he is feeling right now and is really proud of his side. Credits support staff and coach Rahul Dravid who have been working with them for the last 2 years. On Manjot Kalra's innings, he says that knock was special. Praises Shubman Gill for an outstanding tournament and also his pacers - Porel and Mavi. Thanks the crowd for its outstanding support.
Time for the Indians to get its medals.

Australian skipper Jason Sangha manages a smile. Says that he does not know what to say at the moment but is proud of his team as they have grown and grown as cricketers. Credits India for their win and wishes them luck for their future. On the positives for today, he says that his team really tried hard, giving 110 percent with both bat and ball but India were the better side. Praises the crowd for its support and hopes that the Aussies take this as a good learning curve. Is eager to go back home and take some rest. On the emotions in the group, he says that it is difficult to take those but as a captain, his side gave him whatever  he asked. Again, praises India for outplaying them.
Now the Aussie team comes up for its medallions.

SHUBMAN GILL is the MAN OF THE TOURNAMENT. 372 runs at an average of 124 - a hundred and 3 fifties. Is all smiles and is very proud of his team. Says that they are very fortunate to have Rahul Dravid as their coach. On the advice, he says that Dravid only asked him to express himself and play his natural game. On the conditions in New Zealand, Gill says that he enjoyed them very much. Hopes that his form continues and he does well in future too.

Not surprisingly, MANJOT KALRA is the MAN OF THE MATCH. Says that it is a very great feeling and he enjoyed a lot. On the wicket, feels that it was a good one to bat on. Further adds that it is a great feeling to be a part of the victorious team.
Time for the main presentation now. The match officials get their medallions.

Here comes the man behind the success - coach Rahul Dravid. Calm and cool as ever. In fact, he gets irritated with the young blokes celebrating right behind him, into his ear. Is really proud of the boys and even the support team. Says that the effort put in the last 15 days has produced results. On the win tonight, Dravid says that it is a good memory but hopes it is not just one memory but one which defines the Indian lads for the rest of the careers. On the entire backroom staff, he says that they have been together for the last 14 months and the efforts that have been put in are tremendous. Is proud of the way the young kids put on their efforts on the field and it was really heartening to watch.

Riyan Parag gets a mike in front of him now. Copy paste what I wrote for Porel and Abhishek - Excellent feeling, he says. On asked whether he was nervous, Parag says that he was not nervous, but did not think he would get to bat tonight. Wanted Manjot Kalra to get to his century and take the team through. On the final, Riyan expected it to be a tough match and says that it was indeed a tough match but the Indians actually made it look easy. On the pitch, he says it was a good pitch and as a bowler, one would really love to bowl on such tracks.

Simon Doull now gets Ishan Porel to talk something. The Indian speedster is feeling amazed right now. On top of the world, he says. On the win, Ishan puts it to great team work. Credits the support staff as well. On being asked for good luck messages from back home, Porel smiles and says that there were plenty of messages on his phone, back from India. Unfortunately, he could not reply to all but thanks everyone. Credits the bowlers for bowling as a unit and supporting one another.

Abhishek Sharma is having a chat with Robert Key. Says that the Indian team has been dreaming about it from the last year and finally it happened. Adds that the feeling right now is out of this world. Further says that they had plans in place and just executed that. Also says that it is a very great feeling to be a part of the team and cannot explain the same right now. On the celebrations tonight, Abhishek says that it is the best night of their lives.

A great win for India and if we go deep into criticism, it could only be the missed opportunities on the field. Luckily for them, those did not matter. Big moment for Manjot Kalra, as he becomes only the second Indian after Unmukt Chand to score a century in an Under-19 World Cup final. Kudos. Time for some interviews...

The Aussie bowlers could not extract much out of the wicket but one cannot say they bowled well. India did not get much assistance either with the ball but they smartly used their cutters and changed their pace really well, inducing mistakes. Australia were only looking to hit the deck hard and for some swing but never really were they innovative. Only Param Uppal bowled well but it was already gone when he came on to bowl.

To be honest, this was not totally unexpected. India were always the favourites entering the contest and even though 216 gave Australia something to smile, it was never going to be enough if early wickets did not come by. Such was the quality of the Indian batting that they had back-to-back 50-plus stands - 71 for the opening wicket between Kalra and Shaw, then 60 between Kalra and Gill and finally, an unbeaten 89 for the third wicket - Manjot Kalra batting through.

The Indian unit is on the field and running all around to hug the centurion and his partner. Poor Aussie lads. They are patiently waiting for their opposition to finish its celebration. Most of the Men In Yellow are downcast. But now, the moment is of the Men In Blue.
FOUR! INDIA ARE THE 2018 UNDER-19 CHAMPIONS! Their fourth World Cup title. Second in this decade. Full and wide outside off, Desai reaches out and drives it over cover for a boundary!
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
Down the leg side, flicked away for one.

Maiden Under-19 century for Manjot Kalra! In the final of the World Cup! Well played, young lad. Not the toughest of conditions or the most difficult of pitches but he will take this. It is a final and nerves would have played a part. Gets to the landmark with a simple tuck through square leg. Takes his helmet off and celebrates. The crowd and the Indian dressing room is on its feet. What a knock.
The crowd is expecting again. Here comes the man on 99...
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a single.
Outside off, punched back to the bowler.
On middle and leg, defended watchfully.
Field comes in... Kalra on 99...
Outside off, punched through the covers for another single.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Outside off, guided straight to backward point.
DROPPED! The easiest chance tonight. Full nd outside off, Desai drives it straight back to Uppal who just outs it down.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a run more. Keeps the strike. The stand moves to 80 from 94.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! WHACK! A short ball outside off, Desai pulls it over mid-wicket and gets a boundary!
WIDE. A bouncer outside off, Desai lets it go.
A slower ball, but down the leg side. Kalra tucks it through square leg for a run. Moves to 99.
A length ball on middle, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Short and wide outside off, slapped behind point for a single.
Will Sutherland is back on. Jason Sangha and Param Uppal are in his ear. Would be fantastic to see that magic which produces 8 wickets inside 14 runs.
Pushes it towards long on for one more.
Good save. Full and outside off, Harvik drives it trhough the covers where Jason Sangha dives to his right and parries it behind. Uppal quickly rushes to stop the ball.
They have to wait. A tad short, punched down to long off for a run.
Comes down the track and pushes the ball down to long on to bring the man on 97 back on strike. The Indian dressing room is on the edge of its seats...
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! A full toss on middle, Desai swings it past short mid-wicket and gets a boundary. Brings up the 200 FOR INDIA, just 17 more needed from 89 balls. Moves to 32 from 46 balls.
Tossed up outside off, driven past the bowler towards long off for another single.
Down the leg side, helped through square leg for one. Wants two but then changes his mind.
Full and outside off, eased down to long off for a run.

FOUR! Wonderfully timed. Fractionally short, the googly, Desai goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket. Once the ball makes contact with the turf, it speeds away. The stand moves to 62 from 81 balls.
Short and outside off, cut through sweeper for a single.
Very full, around middle, Kalra looks to swing but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.

Final Drinks break of the World Cup. Pretty much a one-sided contest, with only time to decide when the game would be over. Kalra is all set to get to his ton while Harvik can remain not out to see his team home.

DROPPED! Tough chance again. Full and outside off, Kalra comes down the track and hits it straight back. Uppal leaps but can only get fingertips to it. Slows down the pace and hence long off can get to the ball. A single results. 29 more to win.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Outside off, the batsman gets a bottom edge of the bat on that one. They pick up a single.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. Two runs added to the total.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Driven towards the mid off region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Full and outside off, driven through long off for a run.
Full and outside off, watchfully blocked.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
A short ball, pulled away for a single.
Lloyd Pope is back on.
Full again, driven straight back to the bowler again.
Full and outside off, driven straight back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full on middle and leg, eased down to long on for a run. Moves to 90 from 86 balls. 39 more needed for India.
On middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover. There is a slight fumble but they do not run.
Similar length, but the line is a bit too wide. Manjot reaches out and drives it through the covers where it is well fielded. Manjot wants a single but is sent back.
Fuller this time, solidly pushed towards cover.
Closer to the off stump, angling in, tight line, watchfully defended.
FOUR! A wonderful shot. Full and outside off, Kalra reaches out and lofts it over extra cover for a one-bounce boundary!
WIDE. Down the leg side, a tad short, Kalra looks to pull but misses.
Outside off, placed straight to point.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single. The stand moves to 40 from 52 balls.
Jonathan Merlo comes back for another spell.
Short and outside off, Harvik goes back and beautifully places it through the covers for a run more.
The arm ball, on middle and leg, punched wide of long on for another single.
Jumps out, gets to the pitch of the ball and pushes it down to long on for one. 49 more needed for a win.
Wider outside off, driven straight to point.
Full again, driven straight to short extra cover who misfields and concedes a run.
Full and outside off, Desai comes down the track and eases it down to long on for a single.
SIX! WALLOP! Oh dear... that is a full toss on middle, Kalra is more than happy to play that and swings it miles over mid-wicket! Moves to 83 from 78 balls. The stand moves to 34 from 46 balls.
Another long hop, punched past cover for one.
A touch short, landed outside off, spinning away, Harvik goes back and cuts it straight to Jason Sangha at short extra cover.
Full and outside off, defensively pushed towards cover.
Comes down the track, Pope tries to york him, bowls it full and outside leg, but Kalra pushes the ball down to long on for a run. 59 more needed for a win.
Short and wide outside off, slapped through the covers for a single.
Lloyd Pope is back on.

DROPPED! What a terrific effort though. Full and outside off, HD looks to play the slog sweep but hits the ball high in the air. Nathan McSweeney runs back from short mid-wicket, covers excellent ground, puts in a fine dive, but cannot take the catch. A run taken.
Fuller, outside off, driven straight to cover.
Similar ball, once again Harvik goes back to block.
Full again, coming in from outside off, solidly defended.
Outside off, pushed to the off side.
FOUR! Thick outside edge but does not matter at this stage. Full and wide outside off, Desai reaches out to drive but gets a thick outside edge, well wide of short third man and earns a boundary.

Full and outside off, driven through the covers where Jason Sangha dives and makes a terrific stop. Gets up in a flash and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Nearly concedes an overthrow as well.
Outside off, Desai looks to flick but gets an inside edge through square leg. A run taken. The stand moves to 20 from 33 balls.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single to bring up INDIA'S 150. Just 67 more needed from 140 balls.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! Up and over. A short ball, wide outside off, asking for trouble and Australia get trouble. Kalra gets on top of the bounce and cuts it over point for a boundary. 68 more needed for a win now.
On a length outside off, angling in, defended to the off side.
Dragged down, around off, HD goes back to pull but finds short mid-wicket.
One more on that line and length, pushed to the off side.
Full again, compactly blocked.
Full again, outside off, watchfully defended.
Short and outside off, crunched to sweeper cover for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
A big LBW appeal but nothing in it. A length ball, outside off, Desai looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. The umpire spots the edge.
Full and outside off, chipped over cover for one. Moves to 70 from 69 balls.
Landed outside off, steered to third man for a run.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Around off, watchfully defended.

A full toss outside off, driven wide of mid off who throws himself to his right and stops the ball. Cannot stop the single. Australia have thrown themselves on the field alright, but they have not got those many opportunities.
Ryan Hadley is back on.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full and outside off, driven straight back to the bowler who cannot stop it. The ball goes down to long off and a single results. Uppal wrings his hand in pain.
Full and wide again, eased through the covers for a run.
Full and wider outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, pushed through the covers for one more.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Down the leg side, flicked away for one more. 79 more needed for a win now.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Full and outside off, Kalra reaches out for that and drives it through the covers for a couple.
Outside off again, Harvik looks to cut but misses. 2 runs and a wicket from that over, Uppal has figures of 2-0-7-1.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.
Outside off, punched down to long on for a single.
Harvik Desai comes in at number 4, replacing Gill.

OUT! Bowled! A wicket against the run of play. With nothing going Australia's way, India manage to hand them something. A decent nut from Uppal, tossing this up over the eyeline of Gill, expecting him to dance down the track again. The batsman did come out, went for the flick but missed the line. The ball spun back in and hit the top of the bails. Had that missed the bails, the keeper would have missed it too. End of a 60-run stand and guess the two partnerships have done enough. Just 86 more needed from 172 balls.
Full on off, Gill comes down the track and works it straight to short mid-wicket.
Outside off, on a length, Manjot feels for it but misses.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total. The stand is worth 60 from 55 balls.
Pushes this towards mid on.
Full on middle, sticks off the pitch, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, cut through point for a boundary!
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a run.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Full on middle and leg, Kalra stays leg side of the ball and pushes it down to long on for a single.
Param Uppal to bowl his offies now.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a run.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
A short ball, pulled through square leg for a single.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Down the leg side, flicked away for a single.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Jonathan Merlo introduced into the attack now.

DRINKS BREAK. Australia badly need that. India rocketing along at more than 6 an over. This game could be done and dusted before the 40th over. The bowlers have found nothing, just a couple of edges here and there which have not gone to hand. Otherwise, this pitch just seems to have got better for batting.
The batsman guides it to third man. They pick up a single.
Outside off, angled in, let through.
FOUR! VIOLENCE! Short and outside off, Gill spanks it through point and beats sweeper cover!
Outside off, coming in, left alone.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
The batsman has been struck on the thigh pad.
Full and wide outside off, driven through point for one more. A wonderful fifty for Kalra, just his second in Under-19 ODIs.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
FOUR! Full and outside off, Kalra lofts this over mid off and finds the boundary!
A length ball now, whipped through mid-wicket for a run.
Landed outside off, dabbed behind point for a single.
Zak Evans is back into the attack.

Nearly! A short ball outside off, SG pulls it powerfully and nearly hits it straight to Jack Edwards at short mid-wicket! Geez, that would have been a terrific catch had Edwards taken it. Excellent stop. Landed just short of him.

FOUR! ELEGANT! Full and outside off, Gill reaches out and drives it through the covers for a boundary! 100 UP FOR INDIA. 114 more needed from 205 balls. Gill moves to 20 from 13 balls with his third boundary. The stand moves to 32 from 25 balls.
The batsman gets a bottom edge on that one. They pick up a single.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a single. 119 more needed for a win.
Ahh.... lucky. On a length outside off, Gill comes forward to flick but the ball holds back a touch and hence goes off the leading edge. Does not quite carry to Jonathan Merlo running in from cover.
Full on middle, driven straight to mid on.
Full and outside off, driven towards the covers for another single.
It's been driven superbly through the covers. One run added to the total.

A short ball now, the attempted googly, Shubman pulls it towards deep mid-wicket. Jonathan Merlo gets to the ball, them fumbles. Kalra wants the single and is halfway down the track but Gill sends him back. Merlo has no idea and throws it to the wrong end, that too, wide of the bowler.
FOUR! TONK! Full and outside off, spinning away again, Gill reaches out and drives it powerfully with his wrists, wide of mid off and gets a boundary!
Floated outside off, spinning away, left alone.
Short and outside off, placed behind point for a couple.
Outside off, played straight to backward point.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.
A good bouncer, right at the batsman's head, Manjot ducks.
Outside off, punched to the off side.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Outside off, steered to third man for a single. 129 more needed now.
WIDE. Full and well outside off, left alone.

SIX! THWACK! He is coming into his own, is Kalra. Outside off, floated up, Kalra gets down and slog sweeps it miles over mid-wicket! 13 off Pope's first over, signs of things to come? Kalra moves to 42 from 35 balls. The stand is worth 15 from 8 balls!
Full on middle, flicked straight to square leg.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

FOUR! Tough luck for Jack Edwards. Full and outside off, Gill leans and drives it through the covers. Edwards hares across to his right, gets to the ball, puts in a dive but the ball rolls off his body into the ropes. 138 more needed for a win now.
On middle and leg, flicked through square leg for a run.
Full and outside off, driven wide of mid off for a single.

Here comes Mr. Lloyd Pope. After his heroics against England, he was nowhere near his best against Afghanistan. Now he has an even tougher ask. Good batting side against spin, a wet ball, a left-hand-right-hand combination, a required rate of under 4 and 9 wickets left in the tank. Will test his skills.
A bouncer to end the over, Manjot ducks. 3 runs and a wicket from the over. Sutherland has figures of 2-0-6-1.
Excellent yorker, on middle, Kalra digs it out.

WIDE. Bowls this down the leg side, Gill looks to flick but the ball swings a mile away down the leg side. Baxter Holt gets across but it is too much for him and he parries it to fine leg. A single taken.
Shubman Gill walks in at number 3, replacing Shaw.

OUT! Bowled! Stop the press. Australia have got a wicket amidst the carnage. That has gone right through Shaw's defense. Landed on a length outside off, Prithvi looks to defend, almost covering the line but the ball comes back in a long way, goes right between bat and pad and hits the timber. The Aussies are pumped up. They needed that wicket, just to stall some momentum. Only wickets can help them win as India need only 146 runs with 230 balls left in the game.
An inswinger, but a bit too straight, Shaw gets across and pushes it towards mid on.
Fuller and wider outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, Kalra looks to drive but gets a bottom edge back to the bowler.
Outside off, MK waits for the ball to come to him and dabs it to third man for a single. 15 from the over!
Outside off, a rare good ball. comes back in, Manjot fishes and misses.

FOUR! Up and over! Well, all eyes would have been on Prithvi Shaw as to how he gets India off to a start but Kalra is coming into his own now. Three boundaries in the space of four balls. Full and outside off, Kalra leans and lofts it over mid off! Moves to 33 from 26 balls. 148 more to win now.
FOUR! CRISP! Half volley outside off, Kalra leans and drives it through the covers for another boundary!
Outside off, punched straight to cover where the fielder misfields and concedes a couple.
FOUR! Welcome into the attack! Short and wide outside off, Kalra cuts it over point and gets a boundary! 158 more needed for a win.
Jack Edwards into the attack now.
POWERPLAY 2 time. 4 fielders allowed outside the circle till the 40th over, if it goes till then.
On middle and off, punched down the ground past the umpire for a single towards mid off. Terrific start from India in Powerplay 1 - 55/0. Nothing much for Australia. Not too many chances either.
Full and outside off, a crispy cover drive from Kalra but mid off cuts it off.
The Australians are getting frustrated. Plenty of chirping going on, sledging the Indian batsmen. They need wickets and the pitch is certainly not behaving the way they would want it to.
Similar ball, pushed defensively towards cover again.
On a length outside off, punched straight to cover.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Up and over. Pretty expected. A new bowler, final over of Powerplay 1 and openers well set. Enjoy yourself. Full and wide outside off, Kalra lofts this over covers and gets a couple.
First bowling change. Will Sutherland into the attack.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. 11 from the over, India gaining all the momentum.
WIDE. Loses his line, bowls a bumper way down the leg side, Prithvi has no interest in that.

FOUR! And another! Absolute delight watching this guy bat. Gets a full ball again, outside off, Shaw shows his excellent technique as he drives it sweetly through the covers once more to bring up INDIA'S 50! These two like batting together - Shaw and Kalra. 4th 50-plus stand in 5 games! 166 more needed now, from 247 balls.
Outside off, defended solidly.
FOUR! CLASSY! Australia leaking runs now. Half volley wide outside off, Shaw reaches out, gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it through the covers for a boundary!
Full and outside off, Prithvi drives it through the covers where a fielder gets a hand to it and takes some pace off it. Two runs taken.
Searches for a yorker again, bowls an inswing full toss, Shaw calmly drives it towards widish mid off.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a run.
Very full outside off, almost a yorker, squeezed through third man for a couple.
Full on middle, driven straight back.
It has started to drizzle again...
Outside off, punched towards cover where Jason Sangha gets a bad bounce and fumbles. Concedes a single. 177 more to win.
A bouncer on middle, Manjot ducks.

FOUR! Lovely batting. Evans goes for the yorker but misses his length by just a fraction. It becomes a low full toss and Kalra is upto it. Drives it straight back, past the bowler, umpire and non-striker, right to the fence.
Outside off, punched straight to point.
On middle, tucked straight to square leg.
WIDE. Hadley has not quite been able to control his swing. Another one is sprayed down the leg side.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
A bouncer but down the leg side, Shaw ducks.
EDGED, SAFE! Outside off, almost of a repeat of the previous stroke, Manjot pushes at it and gets a healthy outside edge. But it flies wide of first slip towards third man! A single taken.
Outside off, on a length, Kalra plays inside the line and is beaten.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover. Jason Sangha misfields but the batsmen do not run.
Outside off, Shaw reaches out to push but misses.
Oohhh... full and around off, PS looks to flick but gets a leading edge which does not carry to point.
On a length on middle, moving away, Prithvi gets right behind the line to defend.
FOUR! THUNDEROUS! Short and wide outside off, a real loosener from Evans, Shaw climbs onto it and crunches it through the covers for a boundary! 186 more needed for a win now.

Down the leg side, Kalra looks to tuck but the ball goes off his pads to the leg side. They go through for a quick single, the fielder has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Direct hit would have been interesting. India missed 3 chances when they were fielding.
The batsman drives the ball straight down the ground.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They manage to come back for the second.
The ball takes the outside edge goes towards the slip region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Outside off, played straight to point.

1830 local - Hurrah! The rain has stopped, the covers are off, the Super Sopper is done with its drying job and we are ready to play! NO OVERS HAVE BEEN LOST. The Aussies get into a huddle. The lights are partially switched on. Now, Prithvi Shaw and Manjot Kalra walk out to the middle. Ryan Evans to continue, to Kalra. Here we go again...

1810 local - The PLAYERS ARE GOING OFF. The umpires thought about carrying on play, because it does look like a passing shower. But it is too heavy to continue. Should not be too long a delay though. Just a reminder - if we do not get 20 overs in this run chase tonight, we shall come back tomorrow and continue from where the game stopped. Should we resume and have minimum 20 overs bowled and then get a rain stoppage again, we shall get to see the champions tonight itself.
Landed outside off, still pretty wide, let through.
It is getting really heavy now, the rain. The crowd is running for cover.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

WIDE. Ahh... right from the first ball of the 2006-07 Ashes. Full and miles outside off, swings further away, almost reaching first slip. The keeper gets some exercise as he dives in front of the cordon.
On middle and leg, watchfully defended.
SIX! What a hit. A length ball ball on middle, Kalra just lofts it through the line and clears mid on comfortably! The rain is spitting now. But play goes on. 195 more needed from 279 balls.
Manjot Kalra faces the Free Hit. The field is being changed. Fine leg is coming up. Mid on and cover drop back. Wait. More changes. Mid on comes in now, square leg drops back.

NO BALL! Ahh.... Evans has knocked over the bails at his end. The Steven Finn rule, one might say. A short ball, down the leg side, good pace, Shaw mistimes his pull but gets it towards fine leg for a single. Shaw moves to 10 from 17 balls.
Full and wide outside off, driven straight to cover.
WIDE. Oops... full and wide outside off, coming back in, left alone.

A huge appeal from Australia but nothing from the umpire. Loose from Shaw. Full and wide outside off, he chases it away from his body and nearly nicks it behind. The keeper, slip cordon and the bowler appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Jonathan Merlo, who is somewhere in the field, sledges Shaw but the latter gives no response.
Full and outside off, PS drives it towards mid off who fumbles and concedes a single.

Lucky man, is Mr. Hadley. A poor ball, a full toss, that too, on the leg stump, somehow Prithvi misses out, flicking it straight to the man in front of the square leg umpire. Timed it too well, nearly gave a catch.
